ExploreReflection and symmetry

How many lines of symmetry does a rectangle have?

  1. A3
  2. B4
  3. C5
  4. D2

Choose an answer.

Need a hint?

Picture folding the shape so both halves match. Count each different fold.

Answer & method
Answer D: 2

A rectangle has 2 lines of symmetry.

StretchSolids and nets

The cubes have no gaps. How many cubes sit above the bottom layer?

  1. A1
  2. B3
  3. C2
  4. D6

Choose an answer.

Need a hint?

Count every cube first. Then take away the cubes in the bottom layer.

Answer & method
Answer C: 2

6 cubes in all. The bottom layer has 4. 6 − 4 = 2.

For grown-ups

Ideas to practise

  • Reflection and symmetry. A mirror reverses left and right, but not top and bottom.
  • Counting objects. Touch or point to each object once; the last number tells how many.
  • Perimeter. Add the lengths around the outside. Do not confuse perimeter with area.
  • Angles. A right angle is 90 degrees; a straight angle is 180 degrees.
  • Shapes and their properties. Count straight sides and corners carefully. A curved edge is not a straight side.
  • Solids and nets. Follow which faces meet when folded. A face touching another in the net cannot be opposite it.

A game mission has 8 untimed questions. Only the game saves choices and hints. A finished mission earns one launch charge and participation towards the Explorer hull in Star Navigator. The chapter goal is 8 different questions in finished sets; hints and wrong answers count as participation, not mastery. Some craft systems link more than one chapter.

Using the feedback

Learning reports distinguish hinted answers from independent first choices. They consider up to 20 recent different, unhinted questions per skill and level, and wait for at least five before suggesting extra practice. Repeating the same question does not add evidence. Reports are practice evidence, not IQ scores, diagnoses, ranks or predictions of competition results.

Ask the learner to explain a drawing or check with objects too. Choose Explore or an earlier chapter when a step feels too large.
